partners.mechanism_chain: STS (HGNC:11171) —DISRUPTS→ Steroid sulfatase activity (GO:0008375); Steroid sulfatase activity (GO:0008375) —LEADS_TO→ Ichthyosis (HP:0000951); ARSL (HGNC:703) —DISRUPTS→ Cholesterol biosynthesis (GO:0006695); Cholesterol biosynthesis (GO:0006695) —DECREASES→ Desmosterol (CHEBI:30740); Desmosterol (CHEBI:30740) —LEADS_TO→ Chondrodysplasia punctata (HP:0001411); Steroid sulfatase activity (GO:0008375) —DECREASES→ Cholesterol biosynthesis (GO:0006695). Loss-of-function mutations in STS lead to reduced steroid sulfatase activity, impacting downstream pathways including cholesterol biosynthesis and ultimately causing ichthyosis. Similarly, loss-of-function mutations in ARSL disrupt cholesterol biosynthesis, leading to the accumulation of precursors like desmosterol and causing chondrodysplasia punctata. The convergence is on the shared pathway of cholesterol biosynthesis, which is affected by both genetic defects, albeit through different initial enzymatic disruptions.
